subChunks.title: Self-paced orientation: Foundation
subChunks.hookHtml: This orientation turns a large subject into a manageable plan: learn the language first, then build explanations layer by layer.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

Psychology rewards steady sequencing. In this phase you build the vocabulary, biological background, cognitive models, and basic research habits that later topics depend on.

Key ideas

  • Treat the phase as a map, not a race.
  • Keep a learning journal with definitions, examples, and uncertainties.
  • Use retrieval practice after each module before starting the next.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.title: Module 2: The Nervous System
subChunks.hookHtml: Before behaviour becomes visible, the nervous system has already detected, transmitted, and coordinated information.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

The nervous system links body and behaviour. The central nervous system includes the brain and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system carries signals to and from the body. The sympathetic system mobilises energy for threat or effort, while the parasympathetic system supports recovery and regulation.

Key ideas

  • CNS and PNS describe different parts of the communication network.
  • Sympathetic activation prepares action; parasympathetic activation restores balance.
  • Neurons communicate through electrical impulses and chemical signalling at synapses.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.title: Module 3: The Brain
subChunks.hookHtml: The brain is not a set of labelled boxes. It is a network where specialised regions cooperate to produce thought, emotion, memory, and action.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

Brain anatomy gives psychology a biological level of explanation. Frontal regions support planning and inhibition, temporal regions contribute to hearing and memory, occipital regions process vision, and parietal regions integrate spatial and sensory information. Many functions depend on networks rather than a single spot.

Key ideas

  • Localisation is useful but can be oversimplified.
  • Emotion regulation, decision-making, memory, and language depend on interacting systems.
  • Neuroplasticity means experience can alter brain organisation and efficiency.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.title: Module 4: Genetics and Behaviour
subChunks.hookHtml: Genes influence behaviour, but they rarely dictate it. Psychology lives in the interaction between inherited tendencies and lived environments.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

Behavioural genetics estimates how much variation in a trait is associated with genetic differences in a population. Twin studies, adoption studies, heritability estimates, gene-environment interaction, and epigenetics all show that nature and nurture work together rather than competing like rival explanations.

Key ideas

  • Heritability describes variation in a population, not destiny for one person.
  • Environments can amplify, suppress, or redirect genetic tendencies.
  • Epigenetic mechanisms can change gene expression in response to conditions such as stress.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.title: Module 5: Evolutionary Psychology
subChunks.hookHtml: Evolutionary psychology asks whether some patterns of mind and behaviour were shaped by recurring survival and reproduction problems.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

Evolutionary explanations consider adaptation, mate selection, kinship, cooperation, threat detection, and social exchange. The approach can be powerful, but it is easy to misuse when explanations become just-so stories without evidence, cultural sensitivity, or alternative hypotheses.

Key ideas

  • An evolutionary explanation must generate testable predictions.
  • Human cooperation can be studied through kin selection, reciprocity, reputation, and group living.
  • Criticisms matter: not every modern behaviour is an adaptation.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.

subChunks.title: Pathway 2 Outcome: Biology Shapes Behaviour
subChunks.hookHtml: This checkpoint tests whether biological explanations have become useful without becoming simplistic.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core lesson

You should now be able to connect nervous-system activity, brain networks, genes, environments, epigenetics, and evolution to behaviour while avoiding deterministic claims.

Key ideas

  • Biology enables behaviour; it does not erase context.
  • Brain functions usually depend on networks.
  • Genes and environments interact across development.

How to study this module

Read the lesson once, then close it. Try to rebuild the explanation in your own words before you check the notes. Psychology becomes useful when you can move between definition, example, evidence, and limitation.
